title: Talking to the Player

content.title: Your Program Can Ask Questions
content.summary: input() pauses the program and waits for the player to type something.
content.body: So far your programs have just printed things. But what if your program could ask a question and wait for the player to answer? That's exactly what `input()` does. It pauses the program and waits for whoever is running it to type something.

content.title: Using `input()`
content.summary: Put your question in quotes inside input(). Whatever the player types comes back as the answer.
content.body: You put your question inside the quotes, and Python will display it and wait. When the player types their answer and presses Enter, Python hands you back whatever they typed.
content.codeBlock:
name = input("What is your name? ")
print("Welcome, " + name)
content.note: The answer gets stored in a variable — just like you learned in Module 2!

content.title: Joining Text Together
content.summary: Use `+` to stick pieces of text together.
content.body:
When you write `"Welcome, " + name`, Python sticks the two pieces of text together. This is called **joining strings** — programmers sometimes say **concatenation** if you want the fancy word.

**Tip:** make sure there's a space before the closing quote so words don't run together.

content.title: What `input()` Hands You
content.summary: Whatever the player types comes back as text — even numbers.
content.body:
Whatever the player types comes back as **text** (a string). Even if they type a number like `10`, Python treats it as the text `"10"` — not the number `10`.

That doesn't matter yet — for now we're just storing names, foods, colors, and so on. You'll learn how to turn text into real numbers in a later module.

content.title: Try It: Ask Your Own Question
content.summary: Every input() stores a different answer in a different variable.
content.body: Every `input()` stores a different answer in a different variable.
content.codeBlock:
name = input("What is your name? ")
food = input("Favorite food? ")
print(name + " loves " + food)
content.note: Run it and type your answers! Try changing the questions to ask about a favorite game, pet, or color.
